result.title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement
result.summary: Post-training recursive self-improvement (RSI) iteratively improves a target capability, operationalized by a fixed anchor benchmark, through repeated intervention, training, and evaluation. Yet most loops use the anchor's aggregate score as their sole observation, so early gains give way to stalled progress and repetitive exploration. When this anchor-only feedback ceases to reveal actionable gaps, a plateau may reflect an exhausted observation rather than an exhausted capability. We introduce adaptive observation (AdaObs), an observation-side mechanism of harness evolution that keeps the anchor objective fixed while adapting the active observation. At a plateau, a controller refines diagnostic granularity, escalates difficulty, and adds related tasks; validated increments are fused back into training, while every checkpoint remains evaluated against the anchor. Across eight independently optimized anchors in long-context reading comprehension and instruction following, AdaObs raises the mean score from $66.4$ to $73.7$ under a matched data budget, outperforming FixedObs, the anchor-only baseline. The evolved harness further improves the seven-task average on the independent PostTrainBench across two agent backends. These results identify observation adaptation as a missing mechanism of harness evolution for sustaining post-training RSI.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AdaObs：在保持锚点基准与总目标不变的前提下，当训练后自改进循环出现平台期时，由控制器调整诊断粒度、提升难度并补充相关任务，将验证有效的增量融合回训练，从而缓解仅用聚合分数作唯一观测导致的停滞。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心主张「平台期可能源于观测耗尽而非能力耗尽」，与 LVR 中监督信号诊断、证据获取和停止决策的设定可供核查地相通；但该工作不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，迁移线索仅限训练循环的观测设计层面。
